newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Herzog praises Hungary's improved regional ties.
newsitem.headline: Herzog praises Hungary's improved regional ties.

text.p: German president Roman Herzog told Hungary on Tuesday Budapest's improved relations with its neighbours had dispelled fears that the European Union would import regional tensions if it expanded eastwards.

"Three or four years ago when the European Union first discussed allowing new members from central and eastern Europe there were fears that these new incoming countries would bring in tensions," he told reporters after meeting Hungarian president Arpad Goncz.
"Hungary's minorities policy has created a situation whereby these fears...have now disappeared."
Herzog arrived in Hungary earlier in the day for a three-day official visit during which the subject of minority rights will play an important role.

He will visit the German speaking Schwab community in the village of Solymar, near Budapest, and hold talks with leaders of Hungary's other ethnic minorities. Later on Tuesday he will visit the Budapest synagogue, the largest in Europe.

In the last three years Hungary has concluded friendship treaties protecting the rights of ethnic minorities and guaranteeing borders with the Ukraine, Slovakia and Romania, all of which have substantial ethnic Hungarian minorities.

The treaties were seen as prerequisites for early NATO and European Union membership and have now put Hungary into the group of countries seen as most likely to be invited to join NATO at the alliance's summit in Madrid in July.
Talks on European Union membership are expected to begin early next year.

Hungary's parliament finally ratified the basic treaty with Romania immediately after Emil Constantinescu was elected Romanian president last November and included two leaders of ethnic Hungarian parties in his government.
The move has spurred three new agreements in the last two weeks on a joint peacekeeping force, the opening of new consulates and common action to fight organised crime.
Herzog will end his visit on Thursday by touring Hungary's economically depressed eastern region centred around the towns of Nyiregyhaza and Debrecen.
